Hi Priya — answered inline below; attaching our operational checklist (VPC-tenant-handback-checklist.xlsx).

On Mon, Nov 2, 2026 at 10:04 AM Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Clara's questions from Caduceus. ...

Summary (operational):
- Auditable manifest: We provide a delete manifest that includes resource identifiers (object keys, snapshot ids, volume ids), deletion timestamps in ISO 8601, and the operator id who initiated the handback. For Private/VPC deployments we can also include an S3 object manifest and a KV snapshot list when applicable. The manifest is produced within 48 hours of the final erase job. (See attachment.)

- Tombstone / snapshot retention: Our default retention policy for tombstones is 7 days post-erasure job for ephemeral snapshots and 30 days for cross-zone snapshot tombstones unless customer elects immediate purge in the handback order. For customers with geo-replication we perform a cross-region sweep; full tombstone expiration is 30 days from the primary delete event. If the customer requires immediate non-recoverability, we offer an expedited purge (see SLA below).

- Backups & long-term replicas: We enumerate active replica locations in the manifest. For managed snapshot backups that live outside the tenant-owned VPC (e.g., provider-managed S3 buckets), the manifest will also list backup ids and last-known locations; Redwood operations will schedule provider-scope delete jobs. Complete deletion of provider-managed backups may follow provider-specific timelines — we include those timelines in the manifest.

- KMS / key destruction: For tenant-managed keys in a customer KMS, we provide key-rotation and destruction receipts if applicable. For Redwood-managed keys we can trigger key-rotation and mark gold keys as revoked; we then record key state in the manifest. Note: cryptographic destruction may have provider propagation delays.

- Witnessed-delete / attestation options:
  * Standard: Signed operations manifest (internal operator signature + audit log extracts).
  * Notarized attestation: We can arrange a notarized attestation (third-party) that signs the manifest; lead time typically 5–7 business days, additional professional fees apply.
  * Witnessed-delete: We support a customer or third-party observer joining an erase window (read-only view) to watch ops run in real time. This requires a scoped access grant and an NDA addendum; scheduling lead time 3–5 business days.

- SLA tiers (examples):
  * Standard handback: manifest within 48 hours, manifest + 30-day tombstone retention (no extra cost).
  * Expedited non-recoverability: manifest within 24 hours, immediate purge action across regions where supported — additional service fee TBD per GB and provider API costs.

- Evidence formats: CSV/JSON manifest, signed PDF attestation, and (optional) notarized paper copy.

Attachments: VPC-tenant-handback-checklist.xlsx (checklist + examples); ProofOfErase_S3_manifest.txt (sample manifest format).

Notes / caveats: provider-managed long-term backups may include delays out of Redwood's control; we call these out explicitly in the manifest and include the provider SLA reference. Also, legal will want exact wording for "non-recoverability" — I'm providing operational facts here; legal can convert into contractual clauses.

If you'd like, I can draft a short one-page Ops statement we can sign off for high-risk customers.
